question.problem:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $-4$ $-2$ $2$ $4$
$f(x)$ $\frac{1}{6}$ $\frac{1}{3}$ $\frac{1}{3}$ $\frac{1}{6}$
$y$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(y)$ $\frac{1}{4}$ $\frac{1}{4}$ $\frac{1}{2}$

Find $\text{E}[10X+8Y].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{x},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{x}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{1}{6}-2\cdot \frac{1}{3}+2\cdot \frac{1}{3}+4\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{y},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{4}+2\cdot \frac{1}{4}+3\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[10X+8Y] & =\text{E}[10X]+\text{E}[8Y] \\  & =10\text{E}[X]+8\text{E}[Y] \\  & =10\cdot 0+8\cdot \frac{9}{4} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
